approach: Codify the ratified CR-6 keep NARROW: state the recognition rule in CLOSED FORM before deriving scenarios (two interacting conditions — shared-ness and frozen-ness — so the fold rule fires), then draw one scenario per CFG edge.

Recognition rule: for each touched artifact, let D be the spec nodes depending on it; a followup is owed exactly when D contains a node that is BOTH frozen AND outside this mission touched set. Enumerate the three degenerate no-followup cells as the over-fire guard (node-local; every dependent touched in-diff; all dependents still draft).

Route through the EXISTING followup channel — no new channel, no new stage, no new class. Inventing a second channel is the failure this CR exists to avoid, and the source line explicitly says it routes via the existing followup channel.

Do NOT override the existing classifier: backlog by default (a sibling MAY be obsolete — that contradicts no completion claim THIS mission made), blocking only when the sibling contradicts a completion claim the mission itself made.

Containment: ONE followup per shared primitive naming ALL its at-risk siblings, never one per sibling — a widely-consumed primitive would otherwise flood the forge, the branching-factor runaway the follow-up containment bar already prevents.

Keep handoff non-adjudicating: it records the risk and does not verify obsolescence, does not spawn the Warden, does not edit a sibling frozen suite, and gates nothing — the corpus-wide formation lens adjudicates. This preserves the existing does-not-spawn-the-Warden non-goal.
Additive to the @frozen handoff.feature (whole added scenarios, 0 modified / 0 removed) so it self-clears, stays @frozen, and owes no Clearance; confirm mechanically at the gate.

Scope every edit to the follow-up subsection: CR-3 (plan-finalize backstop) is in flight in a sibling ship and also touches the handoff surface, so merge order must reconcile without a content collision.

Headless: self-assert the spec gate by:agent within leash and STOP for Council ratification; never write status, never a by:<name> human-ratification verdict, never relay a judge verdict into a durable record.
